doctrinal_rule: Original English sections were directly examined; scope findings apply to one additional stage per each of 15 cases, not whole stage certification. Opposing-source provenance remains separate. Author quotations through a CDF notification are only book excerpts, not entire original-book verification.

records.bounded_finding_en: Pius XII rejects the claim that sustained continence is intrinsically psychologically impossible and argues that reason and grace can govern sexual desire.
records.not_supported_by_selected_passage_en: This magisterial text is not an empirical study of individual celibates. It does not deny loneliness, trauma or a need for clinical treatment.
records.opponent_provenance_en: The 15-participant priest wellbeing study reports experiences, not an authored attack on all celibacy or proof of causal psychological damage.

records.bounded_finding_en: Pius XI identifies freely given matrimonial consent as constituting an actual marriage and its binding obligations. A present intention to marry later is not already that consent.
records.not_supported_by_selected_passage_en: The distinction between engagement and valid matrimonial consent must also observe applicable canonical form and impediments; §6 alone does not resolve every marriage-validity issue.
records.opponent_provenance_en: The CDF correspondence about Charles Curran does not supply the engagement-specific objection verbatim.

records.bounded_finding_en: Aquinas argues that sexual intercourse outside marriage differs morally from matrimonial union because stable provision for offspring is part of the act's moral order.
records.not_supported_by_selected_passage_en: He does not define every possible chaste co-residence arrangement as fornication; its occasions of sin and scandal require further case analysis.
records.opponent_provenance_en: Pew's US survey establishes that 23% of cohabiters cited relationship-testing as a major motive, not that testing improves marital outcomes.

records.bounded_finding_en: Aquinas treats chastity as a virtue governing sexual appetite through reason and will, so the existence of an impulse must be distinguished from voluntary cultivation.
records.not_supported_by_selected_passage_en: This article does not directly specify which gaze, duration or glance constitutes mortal sin; the concrete line drawn in the debate is a reasoned moral application.
records.opponent_provenance_en: The Planned Parenthood overview of sexual activities does not itself advocate sustained lustful looking.

records.bounded_finding_en: Pius XI explicitly extends conjugal fidelity to deliberately entertained lustful thoughts and desires, not merely physical adultery.
records.not_supported_by_selected_passage_en: It does not determine whether any particular friendly gesture, flirtation or premarital exclusivity agreement is breached.
records.opponent_provenance_en: A general Planned Parenthood relationships explainer is not an authorial defense of deliberately disloyal flirtation.

records.bounded_finding_en: Persona Humana §7 explicitly requires intercourse to be reserved to the publicly manifested marital covenant, not merely to a future intention to marry.
records.not_supported_by_selected_passage_en: The paragraph does not enumerate every form of affectionate touching or non-coital genital activity. Those distinctions rely on further moral analysis; not a direct quotation.
records.opponent_provenance_en: Descriptive Planned Parenthood sex-education material explains techniques but does not defend them as a Catholic moral exception for engaged couples.

records.bounded_finding_en: The 2003 CDF document distinguishes the male-female matrimonial union and its procreative orientation from other relational bonds.
records.not_supported_by_selected_passage_en: The excerpt does not prove that same-sex persons lack genuine love, friendship or commitment. It is Catholic doctrine, not an opponent's argument.
records.opponent_provenance_en: The CDF's 2012 notification reproduces Farley, Just Love p.293 advocating legal recognition and p.295 evaluating same-sex relationships; the entire book has not been independently collated.

records.bounded_finding_en: Canon 1084 distinguishes antecedent perpetual impotence, which invalidates marriage, from sterility, which by itself neither prevents nor nullifies marriage.
records.not_supported_by_selected_passage_en: Canon law establishes that distinction but does not by itself prove every philosophical account of generative-type bodily union.
records.opponent_provenance_en: Farley p.293 in the CDF notification argues about recognition of same-sex unions, but the precise sterility/impotence analogy in this objection is not shown to be her own.

records.bounded_finding_en: Pius XI expressly affirms deep conjugal love, mutual help, and growth in virtue, describing the sharing of life as a real purpose of marriage.
records.not_supported_by_selected_passage_en: This does not negate the encyclical's independent emphasis on procreation and child-rearing; it supports neither a merely reproductive nor a merely companionate theory.
records.opponent_provenance_en: Pew reports love and companionship as major survey responses, not that these motives exhaust marriage's moral definition.

records.bounded_finding_en: Pius XI distinguishes permanent sacramental marriage from exceptional dissolution of certain natural or unconsummated marriages and upholds the indissolubility of ratified-consummated Christian marriage.
records.not_supported_by_selected_passage_en: This passage does not require endangered spouses to remain living together; CIC can.1153 separately addresses protective separation.
records.opponent_provenance_en: Farley's own words on release from the commitment appear at pp.304–305 as excerpts in the 2012 CDF notification; independent full-book review remains outstanding.

records.bounded_finding_en: Canon 1085 prohibits attempted remarriage while a valid prior bond persists and requires the prior bond's status to be legally established; canon 1153 allows protective separation for grave danger.
records.not_supported_by_selected_passage_en: These texts do not themselves determine the facts of a particular tribunal case, and separation must not be mistaken for dissolution or nullity.
records.opponent_provenance_en: Farley pp.304–305 and p.310 in the CDF notification are actual relevant author excerpts opposing strict indissolubility and remarriage prohibition, not evidence that annulment is identical to divorce.

records.bounded_finding_en: Humanae Vitae explicitly says a conjugal act imposed without regard for a partner's condition and reasonable wishes is no true act of love and violates the moral order.
records.not_supported_by_selected_passage_en: The passage is not a procedural criminal-law definition of consent or marital rape, and does not nullify every reciprocal marital moral duty.
records.opponent_provenance_en: A general Planned Parenthood discussion of consent does not advocate the coercive entitlement imputed by the illustrative objection.

records.bounded_finding_en: Persona Humana §9 affirms the objective condemnation of deliberately chosen masturbation while explicitly distinguishing diminished voluntariness due to immaturity, anxiety and habituation.
records.not_supported_by_selected_passage_en: The passage does not prove either automatic mortal guilt or automatic exculpation; personal responsibility requires individual moral evaluation.
records.opponent_provenance_en: Farley's different normative conclusion is reproduced from Just Love p.236 in the 2012 CDF notification; not an independent examination of the complete book.

records.bounded_finding_en: The Catechism condemns deliberate third-party display of real or simulated sexual acts and grounds its objection in chastity and dignity, not only absence of performer consent.
records.not_supported_by_selected_passage_en: It does not name all AI or private marital image cases, nor show that every suggestive image falls under this exact definition.
records.opponent_provenance_en: General pornography/consent educational material does not by itself make an identifiable author an advocate of an all-consensual pornography ethic.

records.bounded_finding_en: Casti Connubii §22 explicitly makes chastity and respect for the divine and natural law duties within marriage, rather than treating marital consent as moral carte blanche.
records.not_supported_by_selected_passage_en: It says nothing directly about private digital photographs, encryption, retention, copying or privacy risks; these are prudential inferences, not an express papal ruling.
records.opponent_provenance_en: A general pornography page cannot serve as a primary endorsement of private spousal recordings; the contrast is an editorial hypothesis.
